text:
Sprawdziłem, jak Drama 3, nowy model do syntezy mowy od @FishAudio, radzi sobie z polskim: łamańce językowe, liczby zapisane cyframi i emocje, od śmiechu po złość. Wszystkie nagrania wygenerowałem lokalnie, na jednym komputerze ASUS Ascent GX10 (układ NVIDIA GB10). Dla porządku: to nie jest reklama ani post sponsorowany, model pobrałem za darmo z Hugging Face.

Co było w teście:
• wymowa: trzy zdania pełne „szcz”, „rz”, „ż” i „ź”, każde czytane trzema głosami, a w jednym z nich data, godzina i cena zapisane cyframi, które model musi sam zamienić na słowa,
• emocje: sześć krótkich scenek, w których nastrój podpowiadają wskazówki w nawiasach kwadratowych, wpisane po polsku wprost w tekst, np. [wybucha śmiechem] albo [zdyszany, łapie oddech po biegu],
• głosy: trzy, wymyślone przez model na podstawie opisu słownego, a nie sklonowane z głosu prawdziwej osoby. Wybrane próbki tych głosów podałem potem modelowi jako wzór, żeby głos nie zmieniał się między zdaniami.

Każde nagranie powstało trzy razy: razem 45 prób, ok. 6 minut dźwięku w niecałe 6 minut pracy modelu (nie licząc ok. 5 minut uruchamiania serwera). Do filmu sam, na ucho, wybrałem siedem zdań, każde w najlepszej z trzech wersji.

Według transkrypcji zdanie o chrząszczu wyszło bez pomyłki w 7 z 9 prób, datę i godzinę model przeczytał poprawnie we wszystkich 9, a cenę w 6 z 9. Słabe miejsca też są: w zdaniu o żółwiu w 6 z 9 prób transkrypcja w ogóle nie ma słowa „żuł”, a w nazwie Szczebrzeszyna w 8 z 9 pojawia się dodatkowe „m”.

Najbardziej podobają mi się emocje: śmiech, westchnienie i zadyszka brzmią dla mnie jak część wypowiedzi, a nie jak doklejony efekt.

Dla firm ważna jest licencja (Fish Audio Community License): użytek komercyjny jest bezpłatny, dopóki roczny przychód firmy jest poniżej 500 tys. dolarów, a jeśli instalujesz model u klienta, ten limit dotyczy też jego przychodu. Udostępnianie syntezy mowy innym jako usługi wymaga osobnej licencji, a naśladowanie głosu konkretnej osoby jej zgody.

Zdania testowe i opisy głosów napisał Claude Opus 5.5, który prowadził całą pracę; ta część działała w chmurze, nie lokalnie.

Drama 3 is open-weight, so we tested whether it keeps its emotions when you shrink it.

630 takes per build. Plain 4-bit fails crying lines 22.6% of the time.
Our emotion-calibrated 4-bit: 14.9%. 24.8 GB vs 38.6 GB for FP8.

text:
직접 쓰는 AI교양 126
직접 써보니 인상적인 음성합성 모델, drama3. 한국어 성능도 자연스러워요

Fish audio에서 drama3라는 새로운 음성합성 모델을 발표했습니다. 임의의 텍스트 태그를 통해 발화의 감정과 방식도 조절이 가능합니다. 오디오북처럼 낭독보다는 '연기 지시'에 가깝게 음성합성을 사용한다고 보시면 됩니다. 특정 대사에만 속삭임이나 강조같은 효과를 넣을 수도 있겠네요

개인적으로 한국어를 기반으로 여러 테스트를 해봤는데 한국 성우가 아닌 다른 나라의 성우를 사용했을 때도 자연스럽다는 점이 가장 인상적입니다. 이전에는 해당 언어에 맞는 보이스를 골라야 자연스럽게 나왔는데 말이죠. 

음성합성도 발전이 눈부시네요

text:
Fish Audio Drama 3 이벤트 & 사용법 정리 (2026년 10월 15일 기준)
이벤트 내용
1. 48시간 한정 무료 Plus 1개월 (가장 주목받는 이벤트)
•Fish Audio 공식 X 런치 포스트에 “DRAMA” (또는 Drama)라고 댓글 달기
•런치 후 48시간 이내 댓글 작성자에게 Fish Audio Plus 1개월 무료 제공
•해당 댓글 작성자에게 클레임 링크를 따로 전달하는 방식
•포스트 시간 기준 대략 10월 15일 16시(UTC) 전후까지 유효 (현재도 아직 열려 있는 상태)
2. 11월 12일까지 지속되는 런치 할인
•API: Drama 3가 100만 글자당 $10 (정가 $50의 80% 할인)
•크리에이터 플랜: 신규 Plus / Pro / Max 플랜 50% 할인
◦월간 결제: 첫 달 50% 할인
◦연간 결제: 첫 해 50% 할인
•엔터프라이즈: 전환 시 첫 달(또는 최대 3개월) 무료 혜택 (문의 필요)

Drama 3 사용법
Drama 3는 감정 연출이 가능한 TTS 모델입니다. 단순히 텍스트를 읽어주는 게 아니라, 연출 지시를 주면 그에 맞춰 말합니다.
1. 웹 / 앱에서 쓰기 (가장 쉬움)
•접속: https://t.co/4Ttlx5P4xE 또는 앱 내 Text to Speech에서 Drama 3 선택
•연출 지시 방법:
◦대괄호로 감정/연기 지시: [barely holding it together, forcing a smile] I'm fine.
◦소리·숨·웃음 삽입: [sigh], [shaky breath], [small laugh]
◦특정 단어만 조절 (태그): Go on without me., , , 등
•연출 지시는 한국어/영어/일본어 등 어떤 언어로 써도 됩니다.
•Uncle Roger 보이스도 공식 제공 중 (직접 연출해 볼 수 있음).
2. API로 쓰기
•기존 TTS API와 동일하게 호출하되, 헤더에 model: drama-3만 추가
•텍스트 안에 위와 같은 대괄호/태그를 그대로 넣으면 됩니다.
3. 직접 호스팅 (Open Weight)
•Hugging Face: fishaudio/drama-3
•라이선스: 연구·비상업 이용 무료, 연 매출 50만 달러 미만이면 상업 이용도 무료
•SGLang-Omni 등으로 바로 서빙 가능
주요 특징
•문장 중간에도 감정/톤 전환 가능
•특정 단어만 바꿔서 다시 생성 (인페인팅) 지원
•멀티 스피커 장면 한 번에 생성
•83개 언어 지원
•Artificial Analysis 발음 견고성 벤치마크 1위 기록
원하시면 웹에서 바로 테스트할 수 있는 예시 스크립트나 API 호출 예시도 정리해 드릴게요.

text:
The useful test for AI voice is how cheaply you can fix the one word that ruins a good take

Fish Audio's Drama 3 lets you direct individual words, place a laugh or pause, and change the delivery inside a sentence. That's more useful to a production team than another voice that sounds impressive for ten seconds

The training choice is interesting. Fish says rewards for matching a reference voice can penalize a whisper, while transcription-based rewards can penalize laughter. Drama 3 instead uses a learned human-preference reward. Optimizing for a clean transcript and optimizing for a performance can pull in different directions

For a game studio or audiobook producer, I'd measure time to an approved line: generation, listening, pronunciation fixes, retakes and review. A low price per character tells you very little if the team keeps throwing takes away

There's a gap between the model and the product today. Fish demonstrates replacing one word while preserving the surrounding audio, but its hosted interactive editing and audio inpainting tools are still in invite-only testing. The editing API is coming later. The public workflow is to change the direction and render again

And open weights have business limits. The community license's free commercial use is for businesses below $500,000 in combined annual revenue with affiliates, with transition terms at the threshold. Offering a self-serve TTS service requires a separate agreement. Downloadable doesn't mean unrestricted

I'd test it on a script full of names, numbers and awkward emotional transitions, then change one line after approval. That's where you find out whether a voice model can become part of a production workflow

text:
More good news for Fish Audio Drama 3! 🎉

Thanks to @_akhaliq for the INT4 quantization and his incredible support, SGLang Omni now officially supports Drama 3 INT4! The quantized checkpoint reduces engine weight memory from 37.0 GB to 20.8 GB, with comparable voice-cloning quality in our Seed-TTS EN evaluation. Making powerful speech models more accessible and affordable to serve is exactly what we love working on.

We've also been working closely with the @huggingface team to expand our Drama 3 Space with a completely redesigned UI. Even more excitingly, the Space will soon run Drama 3 on SGLang Omni, powered by an H200 generously sponsored by Hugging Face! We're truly grateful for the recognition, trust, and support.

Huge thanks again to AK, the Hugging Face team, and @FishAudio for making the model available with open weights. This is what a healthy open AI ecosystem looks like: model builders, inference engineers, and platform teams working together to make great models accessible to everyone.

More optimizations coming soon! 🚀

PR: https://t.co/wm5OsB8Hn0

Space: https://t.co/EUh5Puoexd

text:
¡ADIÓS A ELEVENLABS!

He probado Drama-3 de @FishAudio en mi PC 🎙️🔥

Tengo una RTX 4070 Super de 12 GB y 32 GB RAM

35B MoE de modelo con el GGUF Q3_K_S de Jmica y casi todos los expertos en CPU. Cargando una parte en GPU y el resto en RAM+CPU

Habla español, ríe, se emociona... y todo en local 🤯

Y lo mejor la velocidad:
- 5 segundos de audio tardaron 4 segundos en generarse
- Audios largos tardaban entre x1,3 - x2 más de tiempo. Por ejemplo 20 segundos de audio se generaba en 40 segundos.

Es muy buena alternativa a ElevenLabs

¿Qué opináis?

text:
crazy year for OS text-to-speech, and it’s clearly not the end 👀
BIG release by Fish Audio: drama-3
- big boy: 35B, 3B active, day0 support in sglang-omni
- would have loved a license allowing distillation though 🙈
plain-language direction, mid-line shifts, world-level tags
83 languages

features are cool but the moat isn’t just the weights. It’s that reward model (and the human A/B data behind it) + voice library, not released

text:
Fish Audio 的 Drama 3 是目前可控性很强的 TTS 模型，支持用自然语言直接标注情绪和表演方向，也能在同一句话里切换语气、声线，或只改动单个词的读法。

模型是 35B MoE 架构（每 token 激活约 3B），开了权重，在发音准确度上表现突出，同时支持多角色场景、局部重生成和多轮修改。

演示里用 Uncle Roger 的声音做了一段炒饭场景，AI 可以根据实时指令调整语气和内容。目前已在 ComfyUI、Runway 等平台可用，开源权重也已放出。

noteTweet.text:
Fish Audio 的 Drama 3 是目前可控性很强的 TTS 模型，支持用自然语言直接标注情绪和表演方向，也能在同一句话里切换语气、声线，或只改动单个词的读法。

模型是 35B MoE 架构（每 token 激活约 3B），开了权重，在发音准确度上表现突出，同时支持多角色场景、局部重生成和多轮修改。

演示里用 Uncle Roger 的声音做了一段炒饭场景，AI 可以根据实时指令调整语气和内容。目前已在 ComfyUI、Runway 等平台可用，开源权重也已放出。

text:
@FishAudio just released Drama 3, an open-weight text-to-speech model built for more expressive, controllable voices

you can control how a specific word sounds, change the emotion halfway through a sentence, or switch voices whenever you need to.

that level of control is useful for creators making videos, voiceovers, characters and audiobooks without hiring voice actors for every role.

Fish Audio has raised $52M in seed funding and says it has over 15M users.

now they’re making a model like this available with open weights, giving developers more room to build with it.

text:
Ok, ce que vient de sortir Fish Audio est assez dingue.

Leur nouvelle IA vocale, Drama 3, permet littéralement de diriger une voix comme un acteur.

Tu peux lui demander de parler avec un ton complètement désespéré, de changer d'émotion ou même de voix en plein milieu d'une phrase. Et elle s'exécute.

Mais le truc que je trouve le plus fou, c'est que si UN SEUL mot sonne mal, tu peux corriger uniquement ce mot sans toucher au reste de l'audio.

Tu peux aussi faire jouer plusieurs personnages à partir d'un seul texte, ou cloner ta propre voix pour la faire parler dans d'autres langues.

Et pour leur démo, ils ont carrément utilisé la voix clonée d'Uncle Roger pour lui faire défoncer son propre riz sauté 😭

A couple of months ago, for my new project atlas. (https://t.co/14HVoOd1wE), the application, which helps you travel more interestingly and know what's around you with voice guidance, I asked @ElevenLabs for a startup grant, and they rejected me. OK boomer. 

Now I can use my 2 RTX 4090s with 48 GB of video memory to generate the needed voice guides for free! Thanks, ElevenLabs, for rejecting me, and thanks, @FishAudio, for supporting us with your open-weight models.

Time to build and to make a new public release. ElevenLabs' token prices were incompatible with any reasonable business model I tried.

text:
Drama 3 is open-weight and sits at the top of the independent open-weights TTS leaderboards on pronunciation robustness (93.2%) and the provider voice arena. Pricing on the hosted API is $15 per million characters - well below ElevenLabs v4.

The earlier $52M seed came against roughly $21M ARR and 8M users at the time. The new claim of 15M+ users and the decision to open the weights again (after keeping the prior flagship closed) changes the competitive set. Controllability at the word level is the claimed differentiator; the operational test is whether that control survives long multi-character scenes and voice cloning from short samples without quality collapse or consistency drift.

Open weights accelerate adoption among developers who already ship on ComfyUI, Runway, and similar tools, but they also lower the barrier for anyone who wants to fine-tune or distill the emotion controls. The real constraint is not model quality on short clips. It is whether the hosting economics and the license terms keep enough high-value enterprise volume on the paid path once the weights are public.

Does word-level control actually reduce the number of regenerations enough to offset the lower price, or does most of the volume still come from the hosted convenience layer?

text:
AI 语音公司 Fish Audio 正式开源 Drama 3 模型权重，开发者可以从 Hugging Face 下载并自行部署。Drama 3 早在 9 月就推出了预览版，这次全面开放网页、App 和 API，同时公开模型权重、推理代码和技术报告。

Drama 3 基于 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 语言模型构建，总参数量达 350 亿，每次生成仅激活约 30 亿参数，支持 83 种语言。它主打精细控制语音表演，用户可以直接用自然语言描述情绪，让一句台词从平静转为哽咽，在指定位置插入笑声，甚至让最多 16 个角色在同一段文本中轮流说话。

在 Artificial Analysis 的英语发音准确率测试中，Drama 3 以 93.2% 排名第一，高于上一代 S2.1 Pro 的 88.1%。

Drama 3 采用 Fish Audio Community License。研究和非商业用途免费，个人或企业及关联方年收入合计低于 50 万美元，可以在许可范围内免费商用。但如果将模型作为面向他人的语音生成、克隆或推理 API 服务提供，仍需单独获得授权。

엄청난 음성 모델이 나왔습니다. 게다가 오픈웨이트.

Drama 3는 35B 파라미터 MoE 모델(3B active)로, 백본은 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 기반입니다. 

자연어 디렉션([choked up, crying quietly], 대괄호 태그)으로 감정, 톤, 속도, 특정 단어만 제어, 문장 중간 목소리/감정 전환이 가능합니다.

또한 단어 단위 인필링(기존 오디오 유지하면서 특정 단어만 교체), 멀티턴 디렉터 수정, 멀티캐릭터 장면(최대 16명, <|speaker:0|> 태그) 등의 부가 기능도 제공합니다.

라이선스는 연구/비상업 용도 무료, 상업 사용은 본인+계열사 연매출 $50만 미만이면 무료입니다.

지금 인용된 글에 댓글을 달면 1개월 무료 프로모션도 진행하는듯 합니다!

自分の耳ではすでに人間のMP3データと聞き分けつかないが、それでも彼らの理想からするとまだまだらしい

ワクワクするプロダクトを作るのは作る人の想像力なんだな、と勉強になった

text:
this got me thinking about two things...

open weight models first. i think they're one of the best things happening for builders, because a lot more people can build on a strong model for free. i also think a lot of founders will underestimate what that does to their moat. if two startups can start from the same model on day one, the model can't be what sets them apart. so the winners are the ones whose product gets better the more customers use it.

the second is audio. i reckon AI voice is about to show up in places that never had one, like games, education and customer support, because producing a voice used to cost too much. so many teams will focus on how realistic the voice sounds and spend too little time on how it behaves when someone is confused or frustrated. the more human a voice sounds, the more people expect to be understood by it.

so my view is that open tools give everyone a faster start, and i'd put my money on the product, the relationships and the brand built around them.

text:
Fish Audio Drama 3 is here, and you can already try it on our SGLang Omni-powered Hugging Face Space!

https://t.co/EUh5Puoexd

I spent some time playing with it today. Just upload a short reference audio clip, provide its transcript, and type a completely new sentence. Drama 3 will generate that sentence in the reference voice. Naturally, I tested it with a line about Southern California. 😂 (I deeply love my home in SoCal, Irvine, close to Laguna Beach and @UCIrvine )

Huge thanks to @_akhaliq for helping us launch the Space and working with us to make the UI more intuitive. We went back and forth on the instructions and user experience, and AK was incredibly responsive and helpful throughout the process!

And a massive thank-you to @FishAudio for releasing Drama 3 with open weights. I love seeing powerful speech models become something the community can actually run, experiment with, optimize, and build upon. Open weights and open inference infrastructure are a great combination.

We have also prepared a full SGLang Omni cookbook covering deployment, voice cloning, streaming, multi-speaker generation, and the HTTP API.

Please give our Space a try and let us know what you think. Feedback and contributions are always welcome!

Cookbook: https://t.co/uzzVMGjtuE

GitHub: https://t.co/KAyUTf8BRb

Also, though I've said this several times, I have to say that we spent half a year bringing everything back to life, and I really appreciate everyone along the way.

SGLang Omni team: Chenyang Zhao, Jingwen Gu, Shenggui Li, Richard Wang, Yichi Zhang, Xuesong Ye, Jiaxin Deng, Ratish P, Jiaxuan Luo, Xinyu Lu, Wenyao Gao, Ao Sun, Jintao Quaige Li, Yuhao Chen, Yuhan Zhou, Xuxiang Tian, Ruoyi Zhang, Junnan Li, Yixiao Zeng, Chenchen Hong, Huapeng Zhou, Yang Gao, Chaoye Fei, Yiyang Zh, Kang, Yitian Gong, Yuan Luo, Hao Jin, Yifei Gao, Gaokai Zhang, Lifan Shen, Hui Shen, Kejing Xia, Jinxin Li, Dongming Shen, Jun Liu, Yue Yin, Zhihao Guo, Jisen Li, Ruoyu He, Xuanyi Li, Chenye Zhu, Liang Zhen, Xiaodong Ye, Yizhi Zhen, Kaizuo Li, Chonghan Liu, Wei Guan, Zhuofeng Li

text:
🚨 This is huge. 

Fish Audio just opened the weights of Drama 3, and it's the first open TTS model that sounds close to perfect to me.

Other models can switch emotion mid-sentence. 
Drama 3 is the first one I've heard where it actually sounds right. 

Three tests against Qwen3-TTS, each on one DGX Spark at home: happy turning sad mid-sentence, a sad whisper, and pure excitement. Listen to where the mood drops.

I think this kills ElevenLabs for anyone who has their own compute.

The catch: it's a 35B model (3B active), a 41.5 GB download, and on the Spark it only just keeps up with real time: 10 s of audio take 9.7 s (Qwen3-TTS 7.6 s).

Artificial Analysis ranks Drama 3 Preview #1 among open-weights TTS models and #1 overall on Pronunciation Robustness at 93.2%, ahead of Eleven v4 at 91.7%. Through the Fish Audio API it costs $15 per 1M characters, versus $80 for Eleven v4. Fish Audio also disclosed a $52M seed round and 15M+ users.

text:
Fish Audio is a plugin in Hermes Agent, so your agent can talk with Drama 3:

`hermes plugins install fish-audio --enable`

then `hermes fish login` and `/fish model drama-3-preview`. 

voice replies, read-aloud and voice notes go through it, in the CLI, your messaging apps and Hermes Desktop.

text:
Text-to-speech models receive little attention, yet they are currently experiencing similar breakthroughs: Fish Audio's Drama 3 lets you direct an AI voice much like you'd direct a voice actor: start calmly, then let the frustration creep in halfway through the sentence.

One can describe the delivery in plain language, right down to which word gets the emphasis. A line as simple as "I didn't say that" can take on a completely different meaning.

It supports 83 languages, and the weights are available to download under Fish Audio's Community License, which is super cool :)

text:
This voice AI startup hit $21M ARR in about a year.

Co-founder Shijia Liao, a former Nvidia researcher, trained a voice model and open-sourced it. 

Creators picked it up, started paying for it, and today Fish Audio, launched Drama 3, a voice model that takes direction like an actor, down to a single word.

And it all started on one GPU.

🎙️ AI voice technology is getting more powerful — and easier to build with.

Fish Audio just introduced Drama 3, an open AI voice model that lets developers edit speech like text and control how individual words are delivered.

The bigger investment takeaway? As AI voice becomes easier to develop and deploy, the competitive advantage may shift from building the technology itself to distribution, user reach, and ecosystem integration.

That’s where $META stands out. With billions of people already using its apps and devices, Meta has a potential advantage in bringing AI voice experiences to the mainstream.

The technology is becoming more accessible. Distribution could become the real moat. 👀

text:
I'm building a TTS chrome extension and the code was the easy part

the voice is what kept killing it

AI voices read everything the same way. a joke, a warning, a plot twist, all in that one flat tone

and when one word comes out wrong, you regenerate the whole line and lose the take you liked

fish audio's drama 3 fixes exactly that. 

you can change how a single word sounds and leave the rest alone

you just tell it how to say the line, like you're directing a voice actor

open weights too, so it's going straight into my extension

text:
ai voices sound pretty damn good now. but editing them is still a pain.

you get a perfect take, except for one word.

fix that word, and suddenly the whole line sounds different. now you're regenerating it again, trying to get back to the original take.

fish audio's drama 3 lets you fix that one word without touching the rest.

and instead of messing around with [whispers] and other tags, you can just tell it how you want something said. like you're talking to an actual voice actor.

that's the kind of control ai voice has been missing.

text:
Fish Audio 推出 Drama 3，現在連 AI 配音的哭腔、忍住怒氣的聲音，都能直接用文字控制。

以前用 AI 配音，最麻煩的就是情緒。

明明劇情已經很緊張，AI 還是用平穩的語氣把台詞唸完。想讓角色突然壓低聲音、笑出來，往往得反覆生成。

Drama 3 想解決的就是這件事。

你可以直接告訴它，這句話要帶著哭腔，講到一半突然轉成耳語，最後再用憤怒的語氣說完。

而且不只控制整句話，連句子中間的情緒變化都能指定。

發音也有進步。根據 Artificial Analysis 的測試，Drama 3 在困難詞彙、數字和程式碼的發音測試拿到 93.2%，前代 S2.1 Pro 是 73.2%。

但我更感興趣的是它正在測試的音訊局部修改功能。

假設你做了一段 10 分鐘的影片配音，結果發現其中一個詞講錯了。

以前可能得重新生成整句，再想辦法接回原本的音訊。Drama 3 展示的功能是只修改那個詞，其他聲音保留，連前後的語氣和節奏都盡量接上。

這功能目前還在小規模測試，尚未全面開放。

我覺得這方向很對。AI 配音現在已經能生成相當自然的聲音，但真正拿來做影片，麻煩的是修改。

如果每次改一個字都得重新處理整段音訊，再好的聲音也很難用得順手。

另外 Drama 3 已經開放權重，年收入低於 50 萬美元的個人或企業，在符合授權條件下可以免費商用。

API 也有上市優惠，10 月 13 日到 11 月 12 日，每百萬字元 10 美元，原價是 50 美元。

我現在更想看到的是，這套局部修改功能正式開放後，能不能真的做到只改一個字，其他地方完全不用動。

因為做過影片配音就知道，最浪費時間的常常就是最後那幾個要修改的字。

text:
I've probably wasted hundreds of hours creating content that I only ever published once.

Seriously. Think about how many good ideas just disappear into the timeline after a day.

I recently came across Fish Audio's Drama 3 and started experimenting with something.

What if I could take an old post, turn it into a short video, and narrate it using my own voice without recording anything?

That's exactly what I wanted to try.

I walked through the process in this video, from turning the post into a script to generating the voiceover.

Now I'm looking at my entire archive of old posts a little differently.

No studio. No cast. No sleep.

text:
AI voices are getting ridiculously good. But there's one thing that still drives me crazy.

They can sound perfectly human and still completely butcher the delivery.

I came across Fish Audio's new Drama 3 and wanted to see how much control I'd actually have.

Same script. Same voice. I only changed how I told it to speak.

One version sounds like a casual conversation. The other sounds like a professional tutorial.

And the interesting part? You can literally direct the performance inside the script, right down to specific words.

I recorded the whole process. Listen to the difference.

text:
AI video creation has a big pain point: the realism of character vocalizations. 

They often lack the inflection and emotion that we would see if real human actors were involved.

Fish Audio raised $52M in their seed round to tackle text-to-speech.

Their new open-weight model called Drama 3 allows incredible levels of control. Allowing creators to deliver much more realistic voices for their characters.

I'm going to be downloading the weights to check this model out shortly. Excited that it's open!

text:
FISH AUDIO JUST DROPPED THE MOST EMOTIVE VOICE MODEL I'VE EVER HEARD AND I'LL TELL YOU WHY.

Until now you directed AI voices with tags like [whispers] and hoped it worked.
With Drama 3 you just talk to it like you'd talk to an actor.

Script → Direction In Plain Words → Performance → Fix One Word → Final Take.

→ Tell it "say it like you've given up on life" and it actually does.
→ It switches voices in the middle of a sentence.
→ It voices a full scene with several characters from one script.
→ It fixes a single word without redoing the whole take.
→ It clones your voice and keeps it in character across languages.

They cloned Uncle Roger and it roasted his own fried rice. That's where we are now.

text:
Really cool, open weight, TTS model, just dropped. 

Fixing one bad word in a TTS clip usually means regenerating the whole line, and the take you liked goes with it.

@FishAudio just released Drama 3, it's open-weight,  and the most emotive and controllable TTS model in the world

> lets users restyle single words mid-sentence

> Directions go inside square brackets in plain language, such as “barely holding it together,” and they can be written in English or the user’s own language.

> paired tags such as Whisper, Slower or Forceful wrap only the selected words, so a line can turn from steady to hushed halfway through.

then regenerate the whole take every time one line feels off. on a long script it's brutal

Drama 3 by @FishAudio lets you direct the emotion in plain english & fix a single word without redoing the take

I don't have to refilm individual sentences anymore!!!

voice first & avatars next???

can't wait to see the world when creators get a digital twin

text:
voice AI has always had a directing problem: you either guess which SSML or audio tag like [whispers] gives the right tone, or you keep rerolling until it sounds okay.
Fish Audio built Drama 3 to take performance notes in plain English, so you can direct emotion, pacing, and tone the same way you would talk to a voice actor.
you can also swap a single mispronounced word without regenerating the entire take, or voice a multi-character scene in one script.
in the launch video below, they cloned Uncle Roger's voice to roast his cooking while he makes fried rice.

text:
This is my new favorite way to keep up with AI papers.

I turn my curated papers into a 2-minute spoken technical briefing with @FishAudio Drama 3, straight from Codex.

In the demo, I took one of my favorite recent NVIDIA papers and built a small skill that reads the full paper, writes the script, and sends it to the Fish Audio API with a voice I picked.

What I like about Drama 3 is that you direct the delivery in plain language, like [calm news-anchor delivery] or [slight excitement]. It makes a dense technical summary easy to follow.

Now I catch up on papers on the road or while exercising.

Just incredible how good this is. It has the right levers I can tune to stay engaged with the audio summaries.

The voice you hear in the clip is AI-generated with Drama 3.

text:
Every generative medium eventually gets an edit primitive. Text had one from the start. Images got inpainted. Code you patch a line at a time.

Audio never did. The output came out as one block, so fixing a single word meant regenerating the whole take and accepting that everything around it would shift.

That’s not a quality ceiling, it’s an addressability one. You can’t revise what you can’t point at.

Drama 3 changes a word and leaves the rest of the performance intact. It also takes direction in plain language instead of tags.

A model becomes a tool the moment you can edit its output instead of rerolling it.

text:
Every AI voice you’ve heard this year sounds like a person who was told not to have feelings. Fish Audio is at 15M+ users, up from 8M when it raised a $52M seed eleven weeks ago, and the model it dropped today is built to take direction the way an actor does.

Think about what a voice actor gets in the booth. Hit that word harder. You’re annoyed here, you don’t want to be in this room. Drop the energy on the last line. Studios run on notes like that all day. Text-to-speech gave you SSML tags, which is like handing an actor their notes in XML. Drama 3 takes the notes in plain English, down to one word, and can switch voices partway through a sentence, which is how people read dialogue out loud anyway.

The feature I’d pay for is single-word repair. In real audio work the pickup is where the money goes. One flubbed word in a 40-minute audiobook chapter and you’re booking the actor and the studio again to re-record a line. Fixing one word while the audio around it stays put makes audio editing feel like text editing. Anyone who’s produced a podcast ad or a dubbed episode knows what that’s worth.

Sounding human got cheap fast. Five models in a year, three of them open, 31K stars on a repo Shijia first trained on a single GPU. Once everyone sounds human, the model that can be directed wins the creators and the dubbing pipelines, because those customers tweak delivery hundreds of times a project.

Shipping your best model open-weight at $21M ARR looks like giving the product away. The weights bring developers in. The hosted stack, the latency and the 15,000-voice library are what they pay for once something ships.

The next voice benchmark measures how well a model takes notes.

text:
Grace Hopper spent years being told that computers could only do arithmetic.

Her argument was that programmers shouldn’t have to write in the machine’s notation. 

Let them write something closer to English and have the machine translate it. The field thought this was naive, or a waste of cycles, or both. She built the compiler anyway.

Every interface since has followed the same arc. It starts in the machine’s language because that’s all the machine can take, and it ends in ours once the machine gets good enough to meet us.

Voice AI is still in the first half. You direct a performance by typing [whispers] or wrapping it in SSML, then guessing which tag produces the delivery you heard in your head.

Fish Audio’s Drama 3 takes the note instead. “Say it like you’ve given up on life.” It’ll switch voices mid-sentence, voice a whole scene from one script, and change a single word without regenerating the take around it.

Markup was never how anyone describes a performance. It was just the only thing the model could read.

>No [whispers] or [sighs] tags. You just say how the line should sound
>One script, multiple characters, voices switching mid-sentence
>Wrong word? Change only that word. The rest of the take stays the same

If you've ever regenerated a 3-minute clip to fix one word, you know how frustrating that becomes!
